title: Launch brief (DRAFT) — Signed offline bundles for Redwood Private (air-gapped installs)
linked_artifacts: Linear: ENG-4862 (release gating signed bundle required)
GitHub: redwood-docs PR-1208 (air-gapped installation signed bundles)
content:
Document status: DRAFT (working). This is a launch brief for internal alignment across Product, Release Eng, Security, Support, CS/SE, and Docs.

Owner: Vivek (Product, Private)
PM/Program: Talia Benson
Release Eng: Connor O’Brien
Security: Marcus Lin (Eng), Dr. Aisha Rahman (policy sponsor), Olga Petrov (GRC)
Support readiness: Dev Patel
CS/SE enablement: Rachel Kim / Fatima Noor

============================================================
1) Launch summary
============================================================
What we’re launching
- Redwood Private offline installation bundles that are cryptographically signed by Redwood.
- Installer preflight verifies signature + manifest integrity offline and fails closed on mismatch.
- Includes trust store support (multiple signing keys) and documented key rotation / trust root update process.
- Adds clear break-glass path (policy-gated) that logs prominent audit warnings.

Why now
- Air-gapped customers (defense, healthcare, regulated finance, research labs) require strong supply-chain integrity guarantees.
- Current unsigned bundles create review friction (procurement/security) and increase tamper risk during offline transport.

Release target (current plan)
- Redwood Private 2026.01 (or next Private train if gating isn’t met; see timeline + go/no-go).

Definition of done for launch (high level)
- Signed bundle build is deterministic/reproducible enough for Security sign-off (within stated constraints).
- Release train gating prevents shipping Private artifacts without valid signatures + verification tests.
- Support/CS has a documented install flow, troubleshooting, and escalation runbooks.
- Docs published for customers + internal enablement materials.

============================================================
2) Target customers + personas
============================================================
Primary segment
- Air-gapped / offline installations of Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem packaging, but focus is on “no outbound network” / “controlled media transfer”).

Personas
- Platform / Infra lead (owns cluster + install process): wants predictable install/upgrade and clear failure modes.
- Security / GRC reviewer: wants provenance, integrity, key custody story, and auditable evidence.
- SRE / Ops: wants runbooks for failures and minimal time spent on exceptions.
- SE / PS (Redwood): needs repeatable preflight verification steps and a supportable “bundle report” during pilots.

Known early pilots / design partners (as of now; confirm with PM-907)
- Helios Defense (air-gapped, strict media controls, time source constraints)
- AsterBank (regulated finance, audit log + evidence heavy)
- Northbridge Health (on-prem POC, offline install constraints)

============================================================
3) Positioning + customer messaging (draft)
============================================================
One-liner
- “Redwood Private now supports signed offline bundles, enabling secure air-gapped installs with offline verification of integrity and provenance.”

Customer-facing problem statement
- “When installing Redwood Private in air-gapped environments, customers must transfer artifacts via offline media. Without cryptographic signatures, it’s difficult to prove artifacts are authentic and unmodified.”

Customer-facing value
- Integrity and provenance: installer verifies the bundle is exactly what Redwood released.
- Reduced supply-chain risk: detects tampering, partial/corrupt transfers, and mismatched contents.
- Better operational outcomes: consistent error messages, runbooks, and support bundle capture for faster triage.
- Key rotation path: avoids “bricking” long-lived offline environments when Redwood rotates signing keys.

What this is NOT (set expectations)
- Not customer-signed bundles (no customer-managed signing root in this phase).
- Not a fully general artifact signing framework for all Redwood products (this is specific to Redwood Private offline bundles + installer verification).
- Not a substitute for customer’s internal malware scanning / media handling policies.

Suggested short paragraph (for email/enablement)
- “Starting with Redwood Private 2026.01, offline installation bundles are signed by Redwood. During installation, the Redwood Private installer verifies the bundle signature and a signed manifest of included artifacts (charts, image references, runtime/model artifacts, and SBOM pointers where applicable). This provides offline integrity verification for air-gapped environments and blocks installation if the bundle has been modified or corrupted.”

============================================================
4) Packaging + compatibility callouts (for comms)
============================================================
Terminology (keep consistent)
- “Offline bundle” = the tar/zip deliverable customers transfer into the air-gapped environment.
- “Manifest” = canonical manifest listing artifacts + hashes + metadata.
- “Signature” = detached signature file over canonical manifest.
- “Trust store” = set of Redwood public signing keys accepted by the installer.

Customer-visible requirements (draft)
- Installer version requirement: customers must use installer version that supports signature verification + trust store.
- Offline environment time: signature verification may require reasonable system time (mitigations documented; time-skew guidance included).

Backwards compatibility policy (draft)
- New installers: reject unsigned bundles by default (with explicit break-glass override path).
- Old installers: can still install older unsigned bundles (but we will message that this is not recommended and may be blocked in future).

Upgrade/downgrade policy
- Signed manifest includes version metadata used for downgrade prevention.
- Rollback procedures must reference the compatibility matrix (installer version vs bundle version).

============================================================
5) Rollout plan + timeline (draft)
============================================================
Rollout stages
Stage 0 — Internal dogfood
- Target: first signed bundle RC validated in staging-like environments.
- Exit criteria: verification + tamper tests passing; support bundle includes verification status.

Stage 1 — Limited pilot (2–3 customers)
- Target customers: Helios Defense, AsterBank, + 1 additional (TBD via PM-907).
- Success criteria:
  - Successful install and upgrade in air-gapped environment using signed bundle.
  - At least one “real-world failure” triaged via runbook (transport corruption, time skew, unknown key) with acceptable time-to-resolution.
  - Customer security team acknowledges signing story and evidence is sufficient for their review.

Stage 2 — Limited availability (LA)
- Offer to additional Private prospects with air-gapped requirement.
- Support staffed with updated macros and escalation policy.

Stage 3 — GA
- Signed bundles produced for every Redwood Private release.
- Release gating enforced (no unsigned bundles ship without approved exception).

Current date assumptions (note: adjust as release train moves)
- Week of 2025-12-16: finalize customer messaging + enablement draft (this doc)
- Week of 2025-12-30: run key ceremony + sign first pilot bundles
- Week of 2026-01-06: pilot installs, capture feedback and common errors
- Week of 2026-01-13: doc polish + support readiness + go/no-go
- Week of 2026-01-20: LA/GA decision checkpoint (tie to Private 2026.01 cut)

Go/No-Go checklist (draft)
- Release gating in place (ENG-4862): cannot cut release without signed bundles + tests
- Installer preflight fails closed; break-glass exists and is policy gated
- Trust store supports at least N keys (current and next) + documented update procedure
- Key rotation runbook published and reviewed
- Support readiness complete (macros + runbook + escalation)
- Docs published and validated against the exact shipped CLI outputs

============================================================
6) Enablement needs (Support / CS / SE / PS)
============================================================
Support readiness (owner: Dev Patel)
- Create/update support macros:
  - “Signature invalid / hash mismatch”
  - “Unknown signing key (trust store update needed)”
  - “Not-yet-valid / expired signature (time skew)”
  - “Break-glass request” (approval + logging requirements)
- Ensure Support can request and interpret:
  - `installer bundle inspect` output (or equivalent)
  - verification logs path(s)
  - support bundle artifact that includes manifest/signature metadata
- Escalation routing:
  - Installer verification bugs -> Eng Private Deployments oncall
  - Trust store/key rotation -> Release Eng + Security Eng
  - Customer evidence / compliance questions -> GRC (Olga) + Security (Marcus)

CS/SE enablement (owner: Rachel Kim / Fatima Noor)
- SE checklist for air-gapped kickoff call:
  - validate customer time source constraints
  - confirm media transfer tooling (zip/tar behavior, line endings, antivirus scanners)
  - confirm which artifacts must be included for their environment
  - confirm audit log export needs (SIEM / local retention)
- Provide a “preflight verification” step that SE can ask customer to run before cluster changes.

PS enablement (owner: Bruno Silva)
- PS runbook for onsite/remote guided installs in air-gapped networks.
- Minimal set of artifacts/logs to collect for any failure.

Docs enablement (owner: Elliot Price / Kira Thompson)
- Ensure docs include:
  - exact commands + example output
  - error code reference and remediation
  - how to update trust store in an air-gapped environment
  - how to request exception/break-glass and what gets logged

Training + comms (internal)
- 30-min enablement session: “How signed bundles work + how to troubleshoot verification failures”
- Record session and link from Support runbook

============================================================
7) Customer-facing documentation + artifacts
============================================================
Planned docs set
- Public/private docs guide: “Air-gapped installation using signed offline bundles”
- FAQ: “Common verification errors”
- Key rotation doc: “Trust store updates and key rollover in offline environments”
- Release notes entry in Private 2026.01

Customer-facing proof points (for security reviews)
- What we can state confidently:
  - bundles are signed by Redwood-controlled keys
  - installer verifies signature offline and blocks on mismatch
  - logging/audit events emitted locally with success/failure reasons
  - documented key ceremony and rotation practices available under NDA / security review
- What we should avoid overstating (wording caution)
  - “tamper-proof” (use “tamper-evident”)
  - “guaranteed reproducible builds” (state the deterministic build process we enforce, and the verification semantics)

============================================================
8) Packaging / commercial considerations (draft)
============================================================
Pricing / packaging
- No separate SKU for signing (included in Redwood Private base offering).
- Potential add-on later: extended audit log retention/export features, compliance packs.

Contract / procurement notes
- For regulated customers, signing and verification is often a gating control; highlight as part of security posture.
- Provide a short “security FAQ” excerpt for procurement packets (key custody, rotation cadence, exception process).

============================================================
9) Risk register (draft)
============================================================
Format: Risk | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation | Owner

1) Time skew in air-gapped environments causes “not-yet-valid” verification failures
- Impact: blocks install/upgrade; high support load
- Likelihood: medium (observed in pilots)
- Mitigation: documented time guidance; preflight check; optional diagnostics override (logs explicit warning); improve error message
- Owner: Ethan Park / Sean Gallagher

2) Key rotation breaks older offline installs (unknown key)
- Impact: upgrade blocked; customer escalations
- Likelihood: medium
- Mitigation: trust store supports multiple keys; proactive comms; “trust store update bundle” (if needed); runbook + validation checklist
- Owner: Connor O’Brien / Hanae Suzuki

3) Bundle transport corruption (zip tools, antivirus rewrite, partial copy) causes hash mismatch
- Impact: install blocked; frustration during rollout
- Likelihood: high (common offline)
- Mitigation: clear guidance on recommended transfer + checksum verification; `bundle inspect` report; support macro for remediation
- Owner: Dev Patel / Fatima Noor

4) Break-glass overuse (customers bypass verification routinely)
- Impact: undermines security goal; audit/compliance risk
- Likelihood: low-medium
- Mitigation: policy-gated; explicit audit markers; support must require case ID + approval; follow-up to restore normal path
- Owner: Marcus Lin / Olga Petrov

5) Release pipeline flakiness in signing stage delays Private releases
- Impact: release slippage
- Likelihood: medium (staging flake noted)
- Mitigation: isolate HSM interactions; retries; dedicated runners; SLO monitoring; clear rollback plan
- Owner: Sahana Iyer / Neha Kapoor

6) Customer requests custom trust root / customer-signed bundles (out of scope)
- Impact: sales friction for some accounts
- Likelihood: medium
- Mitigation: documented roadmap item; provide explanation of current trust model and planned extensibility
- Owner: Vivek Kulkarni / Naomi Feldman

7) Messaging risk: customers interpret signing as a full SBOM/compliance guarantee
- Impact: security review confusion; legal exposure
- Likelihood: medium
- Mitigation: careful wording; include SBOM pointers/hashes where applicable but avoid “certification” language
- Owner: Naomi Feldman / Elliot Price

============================================================
10) Launch comms plan (internal + external)
============================================================
Internal comms
- #eng-releases: release train status + gating checklist
- #support: new error taxonomy + macros
- #customer-success + #solutions: pilot playbook + preflight steps

External comms (Private customers)
- Release notes + direct email to affected accounts (air-gapped / offline)
- For pilots: customer-specific rollout email with step-by-step checklist
- For procurement/security: short PDF-style FAQ (under NDA if needed)

============================================================
11) Open questions (please comment inline)
============================================================
- Do we default to “block on unknown key” immediately for all customers, or a deprecation window for existing installs?
- What is the minimum supported “offline time source” assumption we will document (e.g., must set system clock within X days)?
- How will we distribute trust store updates in the most constrained environments (separate small signed artifact vs bundled with next release)?
- What exact fields in audit events are safe by default for redaction (customer wants SIEM export but minimal sensitive data)?
- Do we need a formal customer-facing “key fingerprint” publication process (website, docs, release notes) to aid offline validation?

============================================================
12) Notes to self / next edits
============================================================
- Pull in GA criteria from PM-894 (don’t duplicate inconsistently).
- Align “what’s signed” list with the final manifest schema doc.
- Add a 1-page checklist appendix for SE/Support (copy/paste-ready).
- Confirm final release name: “Redwood Private 2026.01” vs “2026.1” formatting.

Last edited by: Vivek (with comments from Naomi + Connor).
